figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Biosynthesis of oxazole or oxazoline motifs in representative natural products. (A) Cyclodehydratase and flavin-dependent dehydrogenase
involved in the sequential production of oxazoline and oxazole motifs in RiPPs. (B) Cyclization (Cy) domain involved in the formation of
oxazoline in the NRP assembly line. (C) The amidohydrolase NatAM catalyzed the formation of benzoxazoline. (D) The α-KGD DnMT catalyzed
the formation of 4-oxazoline. (E) The fatty acid desaturase homologue IoxB was proposed to catalyze the formation of the indolyloxazole motif in
LIAs based on N-acyl L-tryptophan, which was produced by a GNAT IoxA. (F) The α-KGD PimC catalyzed the formation of an indolyloxazole
motif in PIAs based on N-acyl D-tryptophan, which was produced by the cooperation of D-configuration-specific GNAT PimA and PLP-dependent
tryptophan racemase PimB in this work.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Identification of the PIA biosynthetic gene cluster from the genome ofS. netropsis NZY3. (A) Genetic organization of the PIA
biosynthetic gene cluster in the genome ofS. netropsis NZY3. (B) HPLC profiles for the heterologous expression of gene cassettes 1#, 2#, and 3# in
Streptomyces coelicolor M1154 andStreptomyces albus J1074, respectively. (C) HPLC analysis of the product profile of genetic inactivation and
complementation in the PIAs BGC. Note: the peak labeled by an asterisk (*) is an unknown compound overlapped with compound 4.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. In vivo and in vitro characterization of PimB and PimC. (A) In vivo feeding L-tryptophan and D-tryptophan at 2 mM during the
fermentation of the ΔpimB mutant. (B) Chiral-HPLC analysis of the product types of PimB protein reacted with L-tryptophan and D-tryptophan in
vitro, respectively. (C). Feeding 5a and 5b during the fermentation of the ΔpimA mutant was used to test the in vivo substrate selectivity of PimC.
(D) HPLC analysis of the products of PimC protein reacted with N-acetyl L-tryptophan (5a) and N-acetyl D-tryptophan (5b) in vitro. Note: the
peak labeled by star * is an unknown compound overlapped with compound 4.
